summary: Frontend redesign regression pass (dark cinematic theme). Tested logged-out Word page, logged-in Word + Scene tabs (Little House scene reader), CaptionSearchModal, LoginModal, WelcomeModal (not shown for existing user), Account chip dropdown, /admin (top→bottom, incl. Memberships, Stripe sync, Exports, Users table, Recording queue, My Dictionary, Preferred pronunciations, Hidden videos, Overrides), Payment success/cancel routes, mobile 390px. All screenshots and computed-color contrast sweep (walked ~3000 nodes on /admin, flagged elements with |Δluminance| < 40 between text and effective background). One visual/legibility regression found — CaptionSearchModal video/loading area. Everything else is readable and on-theme.

ui_bugs.issue: The video container uses `bg-ink` (line 184 of /app/frontend/src/components/CaptionSearchModal.jsx) which under the new theme resolves to near-white #F1F2F6. Inside the dark modal (`bg-surface #1A1B20`) the entire aspect-video panel renders as a bright white block until the YouTube iframe paints — jarring cinematic-theme break. The loading state ("Searching real speakers…") and the no-results empty state (line 201) render dark `text-paper/80` on that near-white bg — technically legible but clearly a semantics-flip bug from the token remap (bg-ink was meant to be dark-ink surface in the old palette).

issues: Video-embed area is bg-ink (#F1F2F6, near-white) inside the dark modal — should be bg-paper or bg-stage to match the cinematic dark theme. Same class also breaks the mark highlight (`bg-ink text-paper` at line 28, though currently readable) and any future empty/loading UI in this modal.
Header wraps to 3 rows (~111px tall): brand, WORD/SCENE pill, SIGN IN button drops to a new line. Not broken, just tall — main agent may want to make SIGN IN inline or icon-only on small screens.

action_items: CaptionSearchModal.jsx line 184: change `aspect-video bg-ink` → `aspect-video bg-paper` (or `bg-stage`) so the video-embed frame matches the dark theme; then re-check the mark highlight at line 28 (`bg-ink text-paper`) — either keep it (still contrasty) or invert to `bg-rust text-surface` for on-brand accent.
Optional: CaptionSearchModal empty-state (line 201) `text-paper/80 italic` — once the bg flips to bg-paper, this text becomes invisible; switch to `text-ink/80` or `text-muted2`.
Optional: mobile header — consider reducing SIGN IN button height or wrap pill+CTA on the same row for viewport <420px.
critical_code_review_comments: Token-flip regression pattern: any component still using `bg-ink` as a *surface* color (rather than a text color) is now a bright near-white block on a dark theme. Grep’d — CaptionSearchModal.jsx is the sole outstanding case; all other components use `bg-surface` / `bg-paper` correctly.

PaywallModal.jsx (line 95-96) plan cards read correctly in both states (`bg-ink text-surface` selected = dark on light, `bg-paper` unselected = light text on dark) — no fix needed. Verified by class inspection only; modal not actually rendered in this run because katherine is a subscriber.

WelcomeModal.jsx / LoginModal.jsx / SceneReader.jsx / LaundryListPanel.jsx / AdminPage.jsx / DictionaryBuilder.jsx all render readable text on dark surfaces (verified via computed-color sweep on /admin and screenshot review on the others).

React hydration warning surfaced once: "<span> cannot be a child of <option>" — comes from a `<select><option>...` in AdminPage where an option label contains a wrapping `<span>`. Cosmetic (renders fine) but should be flattened.

rca of the issue: Theme token remap (tailwind.config.js) flipped `paper` from light→dark (#121316) and `ink` from dark→light (#F1F2F6). Semantically `text-ink` (now light) and `bg-surface`/`bg-paper` (now dark) all made sense, but any legacy usage of `bg-ink` as a *surface* color survived unnoticed. CaptionSearchModal.jsx:184 uses `bg-ink` on the video container, which now renders as a near-white block inside the dark modal. Fix: replace with `bg-paper` (or `bg-stage`). Screenshot: /app/.screenshots/03_youglish_modal.png shows the regression clearly.
